candidates.name: nowcasting_benchmark
candidates.what_it_holds: Replication code (R and Python notebooks) for 17 nowcasting/forecasting methods run head-to-head: ARMA, Bayesian VAR, DFM, MIDAS, MF-VAR, midasml (econometric); decision trees, elastic net, gradient boost, LSTM, MLP, OLS, RF, ridge/lasso, XGBoost, DeepVAR (ML). Uses FRED-sourced US macro series to nowcast quarterly US GDP, Q1 2002-Q3 2022 (shortened 2005-2010 demo notebooks for runtime). 35 commits, MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-theme: gives runnable code (not just theory) for MIDAS, DFM, MF-VAR, bridge-style comparisons against ML baselines on a mixed-frequency macro target -- a template that could be repointed at ABNB KPI mixed-frequency nowcasting (nights/GBV target with monthly/weekly high-frequency indicators), addressing gap #17.
candidates.last_activity: not explicitly dated on fetch; repo active as of README

candidates.name: nowcasting-dfm
candidates.what_it_holds: Python DFM nowcasting package extending the FRBNY (New York Fed) DFM framework, with a 'Pseudo-Real-Time Synthesizer' (sp_vintage_generator.py) that reconstructs historical ragged-edge/vintage data matrices and maps real release-calendar timing (e.g. 'first Friday of month') to avoid look-ahead bias in backtests; Numba acceleration, Kalman news decomposition, Plotly dashboards. Ships FRED-sourced US macro example series and two spec files (Spec_US_example.xls, Spec_FredMD_2026-07.xlsx). 115 commits, BSD-3-Clause.
candidates.why_useful: The vintage/ragged-edge synthesizer is exactly the point-in-time machinery gap #4 asks for (reconstructing what was known as-of a date) and directly usable as a harness for mixed-frequency KPI nowcasting with correct release timing -- more mechanically relevant than most MIDAS/DFM repos found.
candidates.size_hint: 115 commits, includes FRED-MD spec file dated 2026-07
candidates.time_coverage: uses current FRED-MD vintages (spec file dated Jul 2026)
candidates.last_activity: spec file dated 2026-07 suggests recent activity

candidates.name: bridgr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package explicitly for classical bridge-equation and MIDAS-style nowcasting: automated frequency alignment (seconds to years), indicator forecasting/aggregation (expalmon, beta weighting), prediction intervals. Ships two example datasets: gdp (quarterly GDP) and baro (monthly business-barometer indicator). 189 commits, MIT license, actively maintained (last update Aug 2026 per topic listing).
candidates.why_useful: Purpose-built, current (2026) implementation of bridge equations -- the exact method named in the theme -- with a working monthly-indicator-to-quarterly-target example (barometer survey to GDP) structurally identical to a monthly alt-data indicator bridging to ABNB's quarterly nights/GBV.
candidates.geography: generic/methodological (Swiss author, barometer example likely European)

candidates.name: midasmlpy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python port of the midasml approach: regularized MIDAS regression using orthogonal-polynomial (Legendre) weighting plus sparse-group LASSO, fast proximal block-coordinate-descent solver, tools for high-dimensional mixed-frequency panel data. Sibling implementations exist in R, Julia, MATLAB. 151 commits, GPL-2.0, last updated 2025-05-15 (33 stars).
candidates.why_useful: High-dimensional MIDAS with regularization is well suited to nowcasting a quarterly ABNB KPI from many weekly/daily alt-data series (Trends, calendar pace, reviews index, FX) without manual factor selection.

candidates.name: midasr
candidates.what_it_holds: The original/reference R MIDAS package (documented in a Journal of Statistical Software article): midas_r (NLS estimation), midas_nlpr, midas_sp (semi-parametric), midas_qr (quantile MIDAS), robust SE and forecast utilities. Includes a /data folder with bundled example mixed-frequency datasets. 522 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Most mature, citable MIDAS implementation (basis for many derivative packages found this pass); quantile-MIDAS (midas_qr) is a route to nowcasting a distribution/range for ABNB nights or ADR rather than a point estimate.
candidates.license: unspecified in fetch (repo has a LICENCE file)

candidates.name: nowcast_lstm
candidates.what_it_holds: PyTorch LSTM library purpose-built for economic nowcasting (targets growth rates of stationary/seasonally-adjusted series), with automatic hyperparameter tuning/variable selection, uncertainty intervals via synthetic vintage generation, permutation-importance feature contributions, and ARMA-based ragged-edge handling. No datasets committed but ships an example notebook+data zip. 90 commits, MIT, v0.2.6, sibling R/Julia/MATLAB wrappers exist (nowcastLSTM, NowcastLSTM.jl, nowcast_lstm_matlab). Built by a UNCTAD staffer for official nowcasting use.
candidates.why_useful: An alt-data-friendly nowcasting engine already designed for irregular/ragged mixed-frequency inputs and synthetic-vintage uncertainty bands -- could take ABNB's weekly calendar-pace/reviews-index/Trends series directly as inputs to nowcast quarterly nights without hand-built bridge equations.

candidates.name: nowcastDFM (CRAN: available)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package implementing the Bok et al. (2017, NY Fed) dynamic factor model methodology: dfm() (EM estimation with missing data), predict_dfm(), and gen_news() which quantifies how each new data release/revision moves the nowcast -- a direct 'news decomposition' tool. On CRAN.
candidates.why_useful: gen_news() is the specific mechanism for attributing a KPI-nowcast change to which input series moved -- useful for building an auditable ABNB nights/GBV nowcast that can explain revisions between alt-data updates, matching the pitch's point-in-time discipline.

candidates.name: rjd3nowcasting
candidates.what_it_holds: R interface to the JDemetra+ v3 (official EU statistical software) nowcasting engine: DFM specification/estimation and news-analysis functionality, GUI-inspired API from the JDemetra+ V2 nowcasting add-in used by some EU statistical agencies. Published by the rjdverse org (successor to EU/Bank of Belgium seasonal-adjustment tooling). EUPL-1.2 licensed, 152 commits, requires Java 21+.
candidates.why_useful: Production-grade DFM/news-analysis tooling used in official European statistics context; could be applied to Eurostat tour_ce_omr or EU consumer-confidence panels we already hold, to build a proper EU nights nowcast with news decomposition rather than ad hoc constructions.

candidates.name: GoogleTrendsAnchorBank (gtab)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (EPFL DLAB) that builds a calibrated 'anchor bank' of pre-computed Google Trends queries spanning the popularity spectrum, then binary-searches new queries against it to get precise, comparable, non-rounded Trends values (bypassing the 5-term-comparison and integer-rounding limits of raw Trends). 217 commits, MIT license. Explicitly NOT point-in-time -- an anchor bank is only valid for the exact months/geo it was built on and must be rebuilt per period.
candidates.why_useful: Directly named in the brief's gap #17 ('anchored Google Trends (gtab)'). Does not fix the point-in-time problem that killed our prior Trends test, but does fix the precision/comparability problem (raw integer rounding), which was a separate defect; worth a documented retry using period-specific anchor banks rather than raw pulls.
candidates.time_coverage: n/a (method; user builds banks per period)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Google Trends already held per CONTEXT.md (9 terms, NOT point-in-time, failed test) -- this is a different tool addressing rounding, not vintage; still novel

candidates.name: scalecast
candidates.what_it_holds: General-purpose Python time-series forecasting library ('the practitioner's forecasting library') wrapping ARIMA, Prophet, LSTM, XGBoost, scikit-learn models with a unified pipeline for transformations, missing-value handling, and model stacking. 598 commits, MIT license. Does not implement MIDAS or mixed-frequency nowcasting specifically.
candidates.why_useful: Not a nowcasting-specific tool but a mature stacking/pipeline framework that could host whichever mixed-frequency model (MIDAS/DFM/LSTM) the team settles on for KPI nowcasting; low priority relative to the purpose-built packages above.
